Short title extent and commencement

ORDINANCE XCVII OF 1996
ORDINANCE XCVII OF 1996
TRIBUNAL FOR DISADVANTAGED PERSONS ORDINANCE,
1996
An Ordinance to establish a national tribunal
for disadvantaged persons
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I,
2nd November, 1996]
No.F.2(1)/96‑Pub., dated 2‑11‑1996.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:‑‑‑
Whereas it is expedient to establish a National
Tribunal for disadvantaged persons and to provide for matters connected
therewith and ancillary thereto;
And whereas the National Assembly is not in
session and the President is satisfied that the circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers
conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:
1. Short title, extent and commencement. ‑‑‑(1) This
Ordinance may be called the Tribunal for Disadvantaged Persons Ordinance, 1996.
(2) It extends to the whole of Pakistan.
(3) It shall come into force at once.

Definition

Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers

2. Definitions.‑‑‑In this
Ordinance, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,‑‑‑
(a) "Chairperson" means the
Chairperson of the Tribunal;
(b) "children" means persons who have
not attained the age of eighteen years;
(c) "Constitution" means the
Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan;
(d) "disadvantaged persons" means
women, children and those belonging to minorities, collectively arid severally;
(e) "human rights" means the rights
relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity of every citizen and includes
fundamental rights provided for in the Constitution or embodied in the
International covenants which may be signed and ratified by Pakistan relating
to disadvantaged persons;
(f) "member". means a member of the
Tribunal; q
(g) "minorities" means non‑Muslims
as defined in sub‑clause (b) of clause (2) of Article 260 of the
Constitution;
(h) "prescribed" means prescribed by
rules made under this Ordinance; and
(i) "Tribunal" means Tribunal for the
Disadvantaged Persons constituted under section 3.

Constitution of the tribunal for the disadvantaged persons

3. Constitution of the Tribunal for the
Disadvantaged Persons.‑‑‑(1) As soon as may be, after the commencement of
this Ordinance, the President shall constitute a Tribunal to be known as the
Tribunal for the Disadvantaged Persons to exercise the powers and perform the
functions assigned to it under this Ordinance
(2) The Tribunal shall consist of‑‑‑
(a) the Chairperson, to be appointed
from amongst the persons who have boen Judges of the Supreme Court;
(b) a
person who has been a ...
Member
Judge
of the High Court
(c) four
persons, including two
Members
women
having knowledge
of,
or practical experience
in,
matters relating to
human
rights; and
(d) four
representatives 'of the
Members
minorities,
including two
women
(3) The Tribunal may co‑opt the
Chairperson of the National Commission for Children, Minorities and Women set
up by the Federal Government as members of the Tribunal.
(4) The headquarters of the Tribunal shall be
at Islamabad and the Tribunal may, with the previous approval of the Federal
Government, establish offices at any other place or places in Pakistan.
(5) No act
or proceeding of the Tribunal shall be invalid merely on the ground of
existence of any vacancy or defect in the constitution of, the Tribunal.

4. Tenure of office of the Chairperson, etc.‑‑‑(1) The
Chairperson shall, subject to the pleasure of the President, hold office for a
term of three years from the date on which he enters upon his office. '
(2) In the event of the occurrence of any
vacancy in the office of the Chairperson by reason of his death, resignation or
where the Chairperson is unable to perform his functions owing to absence on
leave or for any other reason, the President may, by notification in the
official Gazette, authorise one of the members to act as the Chairperson until
the appointment of a new Chairperson or, as the case may be, the Chairperson
resumes his duties.

7. Officers and staff of the Tribunal.‑‑‑(1) The Federal
Government shall make available to the Tribunal such police and investigating
staff under an officer not below the rank of a Superintendent of Police and
such other officers and staff as may be necessary for the efficient performance
of the functions of the Tribunal.
(2) The Tribunal may, subject to such rules
made in this behalf, appoint such other members of staff as it may consider
necessary.
(3) The salaries, allowances and conditions of
service of the officers and other members of staff appointed under subsection
(2) shall be such as may be prescribed.

Functions and powers of the tribunals

ORDINANCE XCVII OF 1996
ORDINANCE XCVII OF 1996

An Ordinance to establish a national tribunal

No.F.2(1)/96‑Pub., dated 2‑11‑1996.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:‑‑‑
Whereas it is expedient to establish a National
Tribunal for disadvantaged persons and to provide for matters connected
therewith and ancillary thereto;
And whereas the National Assembly is not in
session and the President is satisfied that the circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers
conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:
8. Functions and powers of the Tribunal.‑‑‑‑(1) The
powers of the Tribunal shall be to‑‑‑
(a) inquire into, either on an application
trade to it by a disadvantaged person or‑any aggrieved person or on its
own accord, violation of fundamental tights or abetment thereof or negligence
in the prevention of such violation;
(b) visit, under intimation to the Provincial
Government any jail or any other institution under the control of the
Provincial Government where persons are detained or lodged for purposes of
treatment, reformation or protection, to study the living conditions of the
inmates and make report thereon to the Federal Government;
(c) review the factors, including acts of
terrorism which inhibit the enjoyment of human rights, and to recommend
appropriate remedial measures;
(d) review the safeguards provided by or under
the Constitution or any law for the time being in force for the protection of
human rights and fundamental rights and recommend measures for their effective
implementation; and
(e) make recommendations to the Federal
Government for signing and ratification of international conventions and
treaties on human rights.
(2) The Tribunal shall have power to require
any person to furnish information on such issues or matters as, in the opinion
of the Tribunal may be useful for; or relevant to, the subject‑matter of
the inquiry and any person so required shall be deemed to be legally bound to
furnish such information within the meaning of section 176 and section 177 of
the Pakistan Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860).
(3) The functions of the Tribunal may be
performed by benches constituted from amongst the members by the Chairperson.
(4) The Tribunal or any other officer specially
authorised in this behalf by the Tribunal may enter any building or place where
the Tribunal has reason to believe that any document relating to the subject‑matter
of the inquiry may be found and, subject to the provisions of section 102 of
the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act V of 1898), may seize such documents
or take extracts or copies thereof.

Inquiry into complaints

Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers

following Ordinance:
9. Inquiry into complaints.‑‑‑(1) The
Tribunal may, for inquiry into the complaint of violation of human rights of a ‑
disadvantaged person, call for information or report from the Federal
Government or any Provincial Government or any other authority or agency
subordinate thereto within such time as may be specified by it:
Provided that‑‑‑
(a) if the requisite information or report is
not received within the time specified by the Tribunal, it may proceed to
inquire into the complaint by itself; and
(b) if, on receipt of information or report,
the Tribunal is satisfied that no further inquiry is required or the required
action has already been initiated or taken by the concerned Government or
authority, it may not proceed with the complaint and inform the complainant
accordingly.
(2) Without prejudice to anything contained in
subsection (1), if the Tribunal considers it necessary, having regard to the
nature of the complaint, initiate an inquiry.

Tribunal to have powers of the civil Courts etc.

Whereas it is expedient to establish a National
Tribunal for disadvantaged persons and to provide for matters connected
therewith and ancillary thereto;
And whereas the National Assembly is not in
session and the President is satisfied that the circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers
conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:
11. Tribunal to have powers of Civil Court,
etc.‑‑(1)
The Tribunal shall, while inquiring into complaints under this Ordinance, have
the same powers of a Civil Court as are vested in the Code of Civil Procedure,
1908 (Act V of 1908), in respect of the following matters, namely:‑‑‑
(a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of
witnesses and examining them on oath; .
(b) discovery and production of any document;
(c) receiving evidence on affidavits;
(d) requisitioning any public record or copies
thereof from any Court or office;
(e) issuing commissions for the examination of
witnesses or documents; and
(f) any other matter which may be prescribed.
(2) The Tribunal shall be deemed to be a Civil
Court and when any offence as are specified in section 175, section 178,
section 179, section 180 or section 228 of the Pakistan Penal Code is committed
in the view or presence of the Tribunal, the Tribunal .may, after recording the
facts constituting the offence and the statement of the accused as provided for
in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, forward the case to a Magistrate to
whom any such case is forwarded shall proceed to hear the complaint against the
accused as if the case was filed before him.
(3) Every proceeding before the Tribunal shall
be deemed to be a judicial proceeding within the meaning of sections 193 and
228 for the purposes of section 196 of the Pakistan Penal Code, and the Tribunal
shall be deemed to be a Civil Court for all the purposes of section 195 of the
Code of Criminal procedure, 1898.

Statement made by persons before the tribunal to be privileged

12. Statements made by persons before the
Tribunal to be privileged.---No statement made by a person in the course of evidence before the
Tribunal shall subject him to, or be used against him in, any civil or criminal
proceeding, except for prosecution for false evidence:
Provided that such statement‑‑‑
(a) is made in reply to the question which he
is required by the Tribunal to answer; or
(b) is relevant to the subject‑matter of
the inquiry.

Investigation

following Ordinance:
13. Investigation.‑‑(1) The Tribunal may, with the
concurrence of the concerned Government requisition the services of an officer
or agency of the Federal Government or, the Provincial Government, for the
purpose of inquiry or investigation of a complaint or allegation of violation
of any human right.
(2) For the purpose of investigation or inquiry
into any matter an officer or agency whose services are requisitioned under
subsection (1) may, subject to the directions and control of the Tribunal‑‑‑
(a) summon and enforce the attendance of any
person and examine him;
(b) require the discovery and production of any
document; and
(c) requisition any public record or a copy
thereof.
(3) The provisions of section 13 shall, inter
alia, apply in relation to any statement made by a person before any officer or
agency whose services are requisitioned under subsection (1).
(4) The officers or agency whose services are
requisitioned under subsection (1) shall investigate or inquire into any matter
entrusted to it within such period as may be specified by the Tribunal in this
behalf and submit a report to the Tribunal.
(5) The Tribunal shall satisfy itself about the
correctness of the facts and conclusion in the report submitted to it under
subsection (4) and for this purpose the Tribunal may make such further inquiry,
including the examination of the person or persons who had conducted or
assisted in the investigation.
(6) The Tribunal may, in respect of
investigation of matters before it regulate its own procedure.

Persons likely to be prejudicially affected be given opportunity of being heard

14. Persons likely to be prejudicially affected
be given opportunity of being heard.‑‑‑If, at any stage of the
inquiry, the Tribunal‑‑‑
(a) considers it necessary to inquire into the
conduct of any person; or
(b) is of the opinion that the reputation of
any person is likely to be t prejudicially affected by such inquiry,
it shall give to that person a reasonable
opportunity of being heard and to produce evidence in his defence:
Provided further that nothing in this section
shall apply where the character of a witness is being impeached.

Actions to be taken in furtherance of inquiry

15. Actions to be taken in furtherance of
inquiry.‑‑‑(1)
The Tribunal may, on the completion of an inquiry,‑‑‑
(i) recommend to the concerned Government,
authority or agency for initiating prosecution or such other action as the
Tribunal may recommend against a person or persons where the inquiry discloses
the commission of violation of human rights or negligence in the prevention of
violation of human rights by a public servant;
(ii) approach the Supreme Court or the High
Court for such directions, orders or writs as the Court may deem expedient; and
(iii) recommend to the concerned Government,
authority or agency for the grant of such immediate interim relief to the
victim or the members of his family as the Tribunal may consider necessary.
(2) The Tribunal shall provide a copy of the
inquiry report to the complainant or his representative and the concerned
Government, authority or agency together with its recommendations for
compliance within a period of one month, or such further time as the Tribunal
may allow for forwarding its comments on the report, including the action taken
or proposed to be taken thereon.
(3) All orders and decisions of the Tribunal
shall be authenticated by the Secretary‑General or any other officer of
the Tribunal duly authorised by the Chairperson in this behalf.
(4) The Tribunal shall publish its inquiry
report together with the comments of the concerned Government, authority or
agency and the action taken on the recommendations of the Tribunal.

16. Annual and special reports of the Tribunal.‑‑‑(1) The
Tribunal shall submit an annual report to the Federal Government and to the
concerned Provincial Government and may, at any time submit special reports on
any matter which, in its opinion, is of such urgency or importance that it
should not be deferred till submission of the annual report.
(2) The Federal Government and the Provincial
Government shall cause the annual and special reports of the Tribunal to be
laid before both Houses of Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies alongwith a
memorandum of action taken or proposed to be taken on the recommendations of
the Tribunal and the reasons for non‑acceptance of the recommendations,
if any.

Tribunal shall maintain proper accounts and other relevant records and prepare
an annual statement of accounts in such form and manner as may be prescribed by
the Federal Government in consultation with the Auditor‑General of
Pakistan who shall also cause audit of the accounts of the Tribunal.
(2) The audited accounts of the Tribunal 1421X
together with the audit report of the Auditor‑General of Pakistan thereon
shall annually be submitted by the Tribunal to the Federal Government.

21. Power to make rules.‑‑‑(1) The Federal
Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, make rules to carry
out the purposes of this Ordinance.
(2) In particular and without prejudice to the
generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for all or any of the
following matters, namely:
(a) the terms and conditions of appointment of
Chairperson and members
(b) constitution of benches and their places of

subsection (3) of section 7; and
(d) the form in which the annual statement of
accounts is to he prepared by the Tribunal.
